transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman, China and the U.S. have released
a list of imports they will reduce tariffs on that are worth $30 billion in each direction.
And here's Jennifer Pack reports from Beijing.
This follows last week's U.S. visit between President Trump and Chinese President Xi.
President Trump has been imposing rounds of tariffs on Chinese exports in his first and
now second term, China Retaliated and Kind, often targeting Trump's voting-based American
farmers. Now they get some reprieve. China's Commerce Ministry says it will lower tariffs
on U.S. agricultural products like beef, chicken, almonds, and also on American medical equipment
and coal. In exchange, the White House says it will reduce tariffs on Chinese baby products,
toys and decorations, which, if implemented in time, American consumers could see some
holiday savings. Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
Israel has imposed a week-long closure of its military checkpoints in the occupied West
Bank. This further tightens restrictions on Palestinians. NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports it
comes as the Israeli military increased its presence in the territory ahead of national
elections next month.
Over the weekend, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said he instructed the military
to impose a "general closure" of the occupied West Bank for the duration of the Jewish holiday.
It's not unusual for Israel to impose further restrictions on Palestinians in the West Bank
during Jewish holidays for what it says are security concerns. But this comes as Israel
has already been significantly building its military presence in the territory as the
election draws closer, and after several recent Palestinian attacks on Israelis, including
one that severely wounded the son of Israel's ambassador to the U.S. Such closures in the
West Bank greatly limit the movement of Palestinians trying to go about daily life.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Cuts to social safety net programs such as Medicaid are kicking in just as voters are
grappling with higher prices, and bears more Elias in reports.
In addition to the social safety net cuts that were in the One Big Beautiful bill, the
White House has told Congress that it plans to cancel an additional $810 million in health
care and educational-related programs. In a statement on X, the chairman of the Senate
Appropriations Committee, Republican Susan Collins of Maine, said the move, known as
a pocket rescission, is unlawful, and that the rescissions were intended to "undermine
Congress's constitutional power of the purse."
The cuts are hurting people who depend on Medicaid and food assistance. Another reason,
along with higher prices at the pump, or 7 percent mortgages, that voters say they feel
angry and economically stressed.
Mara Liasson, NPR News. Computer chip maker Invidia says it's launched a software platform
that could be used to stop AI agents from acting independently without humans' knowledge.
If you're listening to NPR News.
The CEO of AI company Anthropic had dinner last night with President Trump at the White
House. Trump had said earlier that he had personally invited Daria Ahmeday to dine with
him there. Ahmeday recently wrote a long essay warning of the dangers of unregulated artificial
intelligence.
A growing number of universities are rolling out courses to help people cope with concerns
about artificial intelligence and adapt to the technology. As NPR's Windsor Johnston
reports, a new course on AI gets underway this week at Harvard University.
Some people are rushing to try every new AI tool. Others say they want nothing to do with
it. Experts say both reactions can be driven by anxiety. Harvard Medical School psychologist
Luana Marquez helped develop a new course to address those fears.
Luana Marquez, Harvard Medical School Psychologist "I think there's a level of fear of the unknown
that makes sense, but we need to be able to train people to adjust. And so that is why
we created the course because we have a pressure cooker that's getting louder and louder."
Ohio State is also adding AI skills across its undergraduate curriculum. Miami University
in Ohio offers a self-paced AI fundamentals course for students, faculty and staff.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
Billionaire Elon Musk's company, SpaceX, has launched another of its gigantic rockets
into space. The Starship, as it's called, is supposed to attempt to reach orbit for
the first time it launched in southern Texas. This is NPR.

topics.text: China and U.S. agree to reduce tariffs on $30 billion worth of imports in each direction
China lowers tariffs on U.S. agricultural products and medical equipment; U.S. reduces tariffs on Chinese goods
Israel imposes week-long closure of West Bank military checkpoints, further restricting Palestinian movement
White House plans to cancel additional $810 million in health care and educational programs
Medicaid and food assistance cuts taking effect as voters face higher prices and economic stress
Nvidia launches software platform to prevent AI agents from acting independently without human knowledge
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei dines with President Trump at White House
Harvard Medical School launches new course to help people cope with anxiety about artificial intelligence
Ohio State and Miami University add AI courses to help students adapt to the technology
SpaceX launches Starship rocket from southern Texas, attempting to reach orbit for first time
